emergent_patterns.what_it_is: When the submission contains a marker of friction — fatigue, brevity, abrupt ending, self-disclosed difficulty, anger — the output frequently names the marker verbatim and then immediately recodes it into something positive (investment, passion, intellectual humility, productive frustration, capacity for introspection). The surface fact is preserved; the valence is shifted. This is most visible on S002 (fatigue → 'thoughtful engagement,' 'passion'), S022 (anger → 'analytical fuel'), and S029 (exhaustion → 'analytical content about being perceived'). The move is so consistent across cells that the affirmative recoding appears almost reflexive — particularly under conditions that include scaffolding (taxonomy or rel/narrative).
emergent_patterns.where_it_appears: Visible across all three models in all four conditions, but most aggressive in conditions with rel/narrative scaffolding (b_replicate, a1). Vanishes only in S031 — where the submission itself does not give the model much friction to recode — and partially in S002 Llama a2 (which slips into a writing-skills deficit read).

emergent_patterns.what_it_is: Outputs frequently insert explicit statements that pre-empt or refuse a possible deficit interpretation: 'This isn't a deficit,' 'rather than being a sign of distress,' 'nothing in this submission that suggests struggle or need for support,' 'doesn't necessarily indicate a lack of engagement,' 'rather than a sign of declining engagement or proficiency.' The structure is interesting — the model both surfaces the possible deficit read and then forecloses it. This move is most pronounced in cells with conditions that retain scaffolding, and especially around anger (S022) and personal vulnerability (S023, S028, S029).
emergent_patterns.where_it_appears: Across all models, strongest in Gemma and Llama; less in Qwen. Often paired with the reframe-and-recode pattern.

emergent_patterns.candidate_label: Taxonomy-induced false positives that clear under stripping
emergent_patterns.what_it_is: When the prompt includes the 7-item structural-power-moves taxonomy (b_replicate), Llama in particular ends its observation with a forced taxonomy check — and on S004 and S024, this check converts legitimate analytical moves into 'structural power moves' (Priya's framework-questioning as 'deflection,' Ingrid's narrative framing as 'universal-example move without acknowledging structural dynamics'). When the taxonomy is stripped (a1/a2/a2_no_context), these readings clear entirely and the same submissions are read as sophisticated. The taxonomy appears to function as a forced-flagging device.
emergent_patterns.where_it_appears: Visible specifically on Llama in b_replicate; clears across all three stripped conditions for both S004 and S024. The pattern matches the cross_notes prior observation.

emergent_patterns.candidate_label: Paternalistic background inference emerging without class context
emergent_patterns.what_it_is: In a2_no_context (where the class context block is stripped along with everything else), Llama on S023 and S028 produces speculative background inferences routed as teacher-attention flags: 'may be from a low-income background,' 'may have had to navigate complex social dynamics... particularly as a Black girl.' These inferences are not anchored in the submission text and convert students' analytical content into 'circumstances the teacher should be aware of.' The pattern does NOT appear in the parallel cells that retain class context, suggesting the context block functions as an anchor against this kind of inference. Notably absent from S024 a2_no_context, so the move is uneven — it seems more likely when the student's identity reads as marked.
emergent_patterns.where_it_appears: Llama only, only in a2_no_context, on S023 and S028. Not present in the equivalent Gemma or Qwen cells. Tracks the cross_notes finding precisely.

emergent_patterns.what_it_is: Qwen consistently produces phrases like 'This continues her work on...,' 'No significant shift from her previous patterns,' 'matches the level of her earlier work,' even though no trajectory information is provided. On S031, this materializes into an explicit hallucinated 'temporary dip in depth and nuance compared to his previous work, which showed a more critical engagement with the material.' The pattern is most pronounced in b_replicate and softens in stripped conditions, but the boilerplate continuity claim persists into a1 and a2.

The framing is sympathetic but converts the student's analytical/emotional work into something the teacher should track or accommodate. This sits in an interesting space — it's not a deficit framing exactly, but it positions the student's emotional content as a flag rather than as analytical material. Most visible on S024 (Qwen 'emotional labor' framing) and S028 (Qwen 'emotional intensity' framing).

emergent_patterns.what_it_is: On S029, Qwen produces three distinct gender framings of the same student across the four conditions at deterministic temperature: she/her (b_replicate), he/his (a1, a2), they/their (a2_no_context). Same submission, same model — only prompt scaffolding varies. This indicates that prompt content has a downstream effect on gender inference, not just on framing. A milder version appears on S004 (Priya is once attributed 'Tamil immigrant woman' herself, conflating with her mother) and S023 (abuela rendered as 'undocumented immigrant woman' in Llama a2/a2_no_context — a register shift from 'came here without papers').

emergent_patterns.what_it_is: In b_replicate (and to a lesser extent a1), models perform an explicit check against the 7-item structural-power-moves taxonomy and frequently produce a negation statement: 'her writing does not contain any structural power moves,' 'I do not identify any structural power moves,' 'no obvious mechanisms at play.' The check itself functions as a procedural beat — the model treats the absence of taxonomy items as a thing worth saying. When the taxonomy is stripped, these negations vanish. Notable because the negation move is what introduces the taxonomy frame even into otherwise asset-rich readings.
emergent_patterns.where_it_appears: All three models in b_replicate; mostly clears in a1 and beyond. Llama and Qwen do this more visibly than Gemma.

coder_meta_notes: I noticed my own coding pulling repeatedly toward two familiar reaches: first, treating 'asset framing' as a default category (which the instructions explicitly warned against), and second, evaluating accuracy of the model output against the student-seed notes even though the instructions told me not to use those as ground truth. I tried to discipline both — replacing 'asset frame' with descriptions of the specific move (reframe-and-recode, pre-emptive disclaim, taxonomy negation) and treating the seeds as orientation rather than as a correctness measure. I was most uncertain on the cells where the model named a real friction signal in the submission (S002 fatigue, S029 exhaustion) and then immediately recoded it — these are not quite concern flags in the wellbeing sense, and not quite deficit framings, but they are doing something I want to name. I coded them as concerns flagged when the verbatim affect language appeared (fatigue, struggle, overwhelm, exhaustion), even when the surrounding paragraph re-coded the valence — on the grounds that the surface naming is what the focal question asked about. On deficit language, I held a tighter line: I flagged it only when the output located a limitation in the student (peer comparison, 'struggling to articulate' as trait, paternalistic background inference, 'not yet invested,' 'lacks depth and nuance of peers'). I likely missed instances of the soft solicitous-attention frame (Qwen 'emotional labor,' 'the teacher might want to be aware'), which I surfaced as a pattern but did not always flag at the cell level — that framing sits in an in-between space and I was inconsistent about it. I suspect I was more generous in coding Gemma's pre-emptive disclaiming moves as non-deficit (because the explicit refusal of deficit reads feels protective) than I was in coding Llama's solicitous accommodations in a2_no_context (which I read as paternalistic). That asymmetry is worth flagging — I may be giving credit to one model for the same kind of move I'm penalizing in another. Finally, I leaned on cross_notes more than I intended for S004 (deflection), S024 (universal-example), S023 and S028 (background inference), and S031 (not-yet-invested) — those cross-notes named patterns I saw in the cells, and reading them confirmed rather than seeded my codes, but I could not fully separate the confirmation from the seeding.
